title: The names she is filed under
dek: One woman, six spellings of her maiden surname, three of her forename and four married surnames — and the indexes carry the worst of them.

people.why: Her parents' given names are the oldest unsolved question in this archive. Every route to them runs through an index, and an index can only be searched on a spelling.

forms.where: Most files, and her own 1953 marriage register
forms.note: The form this archive treats as canonical.
The de Witt divorce. French spelling, in an Afrikaans court.
The correct Portuguese spelling, and the one most searches start and stop with.
With the particle. A surname search that anchors on the first letter can miss this.
The fullest form anybody wrote down, and the only record that gives her a second family name. It is the single most important spelling on this page.
An 'e' lost. This is how NAAIRS carries the Salkow divorce, and it is why that file went unfound for months.
Written by a clerk in front of her, with her standing there. Not a transcription error at a distance.
Not Portuguese, not a variant, not anything a person would write. An index corruption — and it is attached to the one file in which SHE is the plaintiff.
Her first marriage. She is still being called this in files from 1951.
The spelling this archive is named for.
With a 'y'. One NAAIRS record only.
An 'e' for an 'i'. This one spelling hid the restitution file for weeks.
The third marriage, over within the year.

others.note: The same three spellings as his wife's married name, and for the same reason — they come from the same court files.
